Re-read the CCC response of 13 July 2026 (planning for a minimum of 2 degrees by 2050, funding falls short, over 2,700 heat deaths in the May to June heatwaves); a search found no Welsh Government adoption of the 2 degree planning assumption by 6 October 2026. The source still stands.

notes: A 2 degree planning assumption is directly relevant to how SI8 defines places that will continue to support health and well-being in a changing climate. Check whether Wales adopts the same planning assumption, since the Climate Adaptation Strategy for Wales 2024 is the Welsh instrument.
summary: CCC response of 13 July 2026 to a new government adaptation package that commits to planning for a minimum of 2 degrees of warming by 2050 with stronger measurable adaptation objectives. The Adaptation Committee calls it more ambitious and in line with its advice, but warns a far more concerted effort and significantly more funding is needed, citing over 2,700 heat-related deaths in England and Wales during the May to June heatwaves.
title: UK adaptation package commits to planning for a minimum of 2 degrees warming by 2050; CCC says funding falls short
